subject.title: [Feature]: Add bounded/validated append semantics for pre-compaction memory flush

question: Should OpenClaw ship strict built-in bounds and dedupe for `trigger: "memory"` writes to `memory/YYYY-MM-DD.md`, or require a more compatible rollout/API design first?
rationale: The source repro is clear, but strict rejection/skipping changes persisted session-memory behavior and a validator hook would create a security-sensitive silent-run boundary.

options.title: Accept strict built-in default
options.body: Land the candidate shape that enforces conservative daily-memory append limits, scaffold rejection, and duplicate skipping before mutation by default.

options.title: Require compatible rollout
options.body: Ask for current append behavior to remain default and make bounded validation opt-in or migration-backed first.

options.title: Pause for API design
options.body: Defer implementation until maintainers choose a plugin/runtime validator contract and security model.

recommendation.title: Accept strict built-in default
recommendation.body: Land the candidate shape that enforces conservative daily-memory append limits, scaffold rejection, and duplicate skipping before mutation by default.

likelyOwner.reason: This is a product/security boundary for the pre-compaction memory-flush feature that this person introduced.
